{{Short description|French mathematician}}
'''Mireille Capitaine''' is a French mathematician whose research focuses on random matrices and free probability theory. In 2012 she was a recipient of the [[G. de B. Robinson Award]] for a paper she coauthored that introduced free Bessel laws, a two-parameter family of generalizations of the [[free Poisson distribution]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cms.math.ca/Prizes/citations/gbr2012.pdf|title=G. de B. Robinson Award|last=|first=|date=2012|website=Canadian Mathematical Society|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=31 January 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Banica|first1=T.|last2=Belinschi|first2=S. T.|last3=Capitaine|first3=M.|last4=Collins|first4=B.|date=February 2011|title=Free Bessel Laws|journal=[[Canadian Journal of Mathematics]]|language=en|volume=63|issue=1|pages=3–37|doi=10.4153/CJM-2010-060-6|doi-access=free|issn=0008-414X|arxiv=0710.5931}}</ref> She received her PhD in 1996 from [[Paul Sabatier University]], where she was advised by Michel Ledoux.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=95884}}</ref> She is currently a researcher for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS), associated with the Toulouse Institute of Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/spip.php?article609&lang=en|title=Institut de Mathématiques de Toulouse - Members|website=www.math.univ-toulouse.fr|access-date=2020-01-31}}</ref>
